domain_restrictions: The inequality 0 <= a <= b must hold.
I is the set of integers strictly bigger than a and at most b.
S is a polynomial ring over the rational numbers with b variables.
R is a polynomial ring over the rational numbers with one variable for each index in I.
The grading is weighted, with degree of y_i equal to i and degree of x_s equal to s.
The ideal generated by y_1 through y_a is homogeneous, so the quotient inherits a grading.
When a = b, the index set I is empty, so R has no generators and is just Q.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b, the weighted polynomial ring over Q in y_1 through y_b, after quotienting by the ideal generated by y_1 through y_a, is canonically the same graded Q-algebra as the weighted polynomial ring over Q in the remaining variables indexed by a+1 through b. The identification sends the class of each surviving y_s to x_s, preserves weighted degree, and carries homogeneous regular sequences to homogeneous regular sequences. If a = b, both sides reduce to Q.
quantifier_order: For all integers a and b satisfying 0 <= a <= b.
Define I as the integers from a+1 through b.
Define S and R as weighted polynomial rings over Q with the stated generators and degrees.
There exists a canonical graded Q-algebra isomorphism from S modulo the ideal generated by y_1 through y_a to R, determined by sending the class of y_s to x_s for each s in I.
Under this identification, homogeneous regular sequences correspond and weighted degrees are preserved.
In the special case a = b, both rings are Q.

witness_dependencies: The canonical isomorphism depends on the chosen parameters a and b through the index set I.
Its action on generators is completely determined by the images of the classes of y_s for s in I.
No extra choice is required beyond the parameters, since the map is forced by the generator assignment.
The preservation of homogeneous regular sequences is induced by the same graded isomorphism and does not require an additional witness.

statement_nl: Let a and b be integers with 0 <= a <= b. Put I := {a+1,...,b}, let S := Q[y_1,...,y_b] with weighted grading deg(y_i)=i, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] with weighted grading deg(x_s)=s. Then the quotient S/(y_1,...,y_a) is canonically isomorphic to R as a graded Q-algebra, via the map sending the class of y_s to x_s for each s in I. Under this graded isomorphism, homogeneous regular sequences correspond and weighted degrees are preserved. When a=b, both rings are Q.
